title: Knowing People: The Personal Use of Social Psychology
author: Michael J. Lovaglia
target_audience: General readers interested in understanding themselves and others
Students beginning studies in psychology or related fields
Individuals seeking practical applications of social psychology for everyday life
Professionals interested in interpersonal relations and group dynamics
core_themes: Influence of social forces on individual behavior
Interpretation of motives—our own and others’
Practical application of social psychology to daily life
primary_purpose: To show how the principles and findings of social psychology can be directly applied to enhance personal relationships, self-knowledge, and understanding of the social world.

structure_format.narrative_style: Conversational, anecdotal, and accessible; uses real-life stories and examples
structure_format.organization: Organized by thematic chapters that explore major social psychology concepts (such as impression management, persuasion, attribution, attitudes) and their personal implications
features: Focus on real-world application over academic jargon

key_concepts_lessons: People’s behavior can often be explained by situational factors rather than personality alone.
Impression management is a crucial component of social interaction.
Cognitive biases affect how we interpret others’ behavior and our own.
Conformity and obedience shape group dynamics and personal choices.
Humans have a fundamental need for social belonging, which affects individual preferences and actions.
Knowledge of social psychological principles can help foster empathy and better communication.
notable_features: Connects classic and contemporary research to everyday life
Focuses on the personal relevance of academic findings
Short chapter-ending exercises for reflection and application
Written to be easily understood by readers with no prior psychology background
cultural_historical_context: Written in the late 1990s, reflecting increased public interest in applying psychological science to improve everyday life and self-understanding. It capitalizes on the late 20th-century trend of making academic insights accessible and useful for a lay audience.
reception_impact: Praised by instructors for its accessibility and relevance in introductory social psychology courses
Well-received as a supplemental or personal growth book for non-specialists
Appreciated for its conversational tone and real-world examples
Not widely cited as a research text but recognized for its educational and self-help value
comparable_titles: Influence: The Psychology of Persuasion by Robert Cialdini
The Social Animal by Elliot Aronson
Social Psychology: Understanding Human Interaction by Robert A. Baron and Donn Byrne
